record.description: One member of this family, TrmB, has been shown to be a sugar-specific transcriptional regulator of the trehalose/maltose ABC transporter [[cite:PUB00015607]] in Thermococcus litoralis.

evidence.explanation: The original cloning methods identify T. litoralis chromosomal DNA and C-terminal His6 pSL152; full inserted sequence was not independently inspected.
Methods calls the same plasmid PF1743 and Chapter 7 uses supplied mutant plasmids; complete inserts and mutant-specific folding controls remain unresolved.
Reported V161A and inconsistent C-terminal tails disagree with the 3QPH sequence and actual Val161 atoms. No silent sequence correction or neutrality assumption is made.

discussions.notes: See all five PF01978 ledgers for reference, construct and assay provenance. Q8U4G4 sequence version 1/entry 96 maps PF01978 to 10-77; TrmBL1 E40/D50 are inside it, but E81/E85/D86 are outside. ED85AA is a double perturbation, not two independently tested causes. Materials list VC1 and the methods report sending mutant plasmids for sequencing, but complete physical inserts remain independently unverified. Thesis pCS19/C-terminal His6 differs from the 2007 transcription preparation; FBPase cloning sites disagree. No isolated-domain sufficiency or atomic DNA contact is asserted. Lee2007 Y49 also maps inside PF01978; pSL242 mutants carry C-terminal His6, while general WT DNA assays use N-terminal His6. The Figure 10 WT comparator tag and assay-specific tags for SEC and radioligand binding remain unresolved.
discussions.prompt: Resolve complete constructs and distinguish PF01978-dependent effects from other-domain and whole-protein effects.
discussions.rationale: Q7LYW4 and Q9HGZ9 have identical reference bodies and PF01978 at 11-77, but the pSL152 species attribution differs between Lee2003 and the Surma thesis. Y50 is within PF01978; E87 and the sugar-binding domains are not. Reference equivalence cannot establish identical experimental inserts or strains.

evidence.explanation: Figures 6 and 8 describe different trehalose effects; original figure images were not available through the attempted access routes.

Methods pp.39-41 and Figures 18-23, 32-35, 45-48 and 51 retain glucose carryover, residual/nonmonotonic activity, unmatched buffers or nuclease amounts and diffuse shifts. Figure 22B retains 2% signal despite zero-output prose; Figure 35 tables contradict blanket below-10% wording. These prevent exact affinity, stoichiometry and atomic-contact claims.

discussions.notes: Obtain stock compositions, active fractions, replicate/error estimates and direct occupancy/competition measurements. Retain prior residuals, nonmonotonicity, Figure 20 percentage-point distinction and Figure 28/41-43 discrepancies. Figure 52 requires same-dose and panel-specific WT controls; some nominally complete repression retains 8/12/10. Figure 53 has template-label and 25/30 ng DNA conflicts. Figure 54 WT/mutant comparisons match nuclease dose even though no-protein lanes do not. Own-promoter EMSA/footprints failed through aggregation; that is not measured loss of mutant binding. See all five ledgers; no uniform inhibition, stable activation or native flux claim is made. The fifth ledger retains Lee2007's reported maltotriose competition, not a fitted Kd/Km; Results fructose versus Methods sucrose remains conflicting. SEC apparent mass is not measured subunit stoichiometry. Original 2007 figure images were not inspected.
discussions.prompt: Resolve preparation carryover and assay-specific outcomes before assigning a single sugar-to-DNA regulatory mechanism.
discussions.rationale: Trehalose relieves transcriptional repression but increases region-1 EMSA retardation under different conditions. The thesis stores proteins in glucose-containing buffer without dialysis; no-added-sugar assays are not established sugar-free. Y50N and E87A retain concentration-dependent repression.

evidence.explanation: Figures 18-23 and 32-35 support scoped TrmB contexts. Independently mapped TrmBL1 Figures 25-31 and 36-43 retain wild-type contexts; Figures 52-54 now add same-dose mutant transcription, EMSA and footprint effects with separate regional hypotheses. Remaining original primary-paper experiments, paralogs and native-cell results still require assessment.

The sucrose-bound structure lacks DNA, while its maltose comparator lacks residues 2-109. Proposed allosteric motion is not directly observed and older/unpublished assays are not new measurements in this paper.

discussions.notes: Inspect full Lee2005 and differential-signals Lee2007 sources, complete the separate PF0124 paper's original mutant/oligomerization/sugar-binding experiments, and assess Tgr/TrmBL2/4 and other taxa without transferring endpoints by similarity. Thesis E40N/D50N/E81A/ED85AA assays are now scoped separately; Y49N from the 2007 paper is not D50N. PF0124 is a target promoter in the TrmB graphs and the tested regulator in the TrmBL1 graphs.
